def git(cwd, *argv):
            subprocess.run(["git", *argv], cwd=str(cwd), check=True,
                           capture_output=True)

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = pathlib.Path(temporary)
            host = root / "vm-feasibility.py"
            guest = root / "vm-guest-probe.py"
            host.write_bytes(b"host bytes\n")
            guest.write_bytes(b"guest bytes\n")
            git(root, "init", "-q")
            git(root, "-c", "user.email=probe@example.com",
                "-c", "user.name=probe", "add", ".")
            git(root, "-c", "user.email=probe@example.com",
                "-c", "user.name=probe", "commit", "-q", "--no-verify",
                "-m", "probe")
evidence.reason: At the pinned tip the real-commit fixture still runs Git through subprocess.run with the caller’s inherited environment and no signing or hook isolation. The commit uses only --no-verify, which does not disable commit.gpgSign or prepare-commit-msg hooks, and inherited GIT_DIR can redirect the fixture commands. So the test remains configuration-dependent and can fail before verify_source_scripts runs.
